A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLoRA, and their readable text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. v1 ends after the references despite referring to an appendix; v2 includes Appendices A-C. Newly supplied appendix content can be identified, without assuming that every underlying experiment was newly performed.

before.justification: v1 reports original ConvNeXt-V2-L, InternViT-6B and DeBERTaV3-base experiments in Tables 1-3, alongside rank, scaling, feature-amplification and training-cost analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and reports additional multimodal, commonsense-reasoning, VTAB and image-generation outcomes, including results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The N-dimensional core-tensor update, convolutional factorization, linear update AGBT and initialization remain unchanged. v1 Equations 5-7 correspond to v2 Equations 4-6. Reframing decomposition as adaptation and specifying experimental target layers do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendices A.2-A.3 add eight commonsense-reasoning datasets and the 19-task VTAB-1K benchmark, substantially expanding task and domain coverage. Appendix A.1 specifies Pokemon BLIP style adaptation for the diffusion experiment only briefly mentioned in v1. The seven visual-instruction benchmarks were already described in v1.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1-3 remain unchanged. New comparisons include ChatGPT in Table 7 and last-layer tuning, VPT-Shallow/Deep, NOAH, SSF, AdaptFormer, FACT-TT and Compacter in Table 8, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives. LoTR and SuperLoRA receive discussion but no reported comparative evaluation.

E3.justification: New protocols include pooled Commonsense170K training with separate task tests and ViT-B/16 evaluation using all 1,000 VTAB training/validation examples with unnormalized inputs. Existing reported settings also change: adapter widths narrow from {8,16,32,64} to {32,64}, and AdaLoRA's maximum budget changes from 567 to 576. These revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2.4 and Figure 7 extend the update-norm and feature-amplification diagnostic to DeBERTaV3-large on SST-2 at rank 8. This provides an additional check of the proposed explanation. The original rank and scale sensitivity studies, CoLA diagnostic and training-cost comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 adds per-task ± values for adapter and low-rank methods where v1 reported means alone. Both versions already specify five NLP runs and pairwise t-tests at 0.05, so this is additional uncertainty reporting, not an established increase in repetitions. The ± statistic is not explicitly identified.

E6.justification: v2 adds seven-benchmark LLaVA results in Table 4, commonsense results in Table 7, VTAB results in Table 8 and generation examples in Figure 6. Newly reported averages include FLoRA/DoRA at 85.6/85.0 on commonsense tasks and FLoRA/FACT-TT at 77.3/76.7 on VTAB. Central scores in Tables 1-3 and the renumbered training-cost table are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 introduces an optimal-update formulation and the pseudoinverse argument G = A†ΔW*B† to support claims about unconstrained factors and reaching optimal updates. This substantially extends and revises v1's brief orthogonality argument. The Tucker identities and method equations remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: a unified low-rank adaptation across parameter-space dimensions, preservation of structural integrity and strong performance across CV, NLP and multimodal tasks. The new title and adaptation terminology do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 replaces explanations based on strong orthogonality with matrix-pattern constraints. Appendix B.2 develops a stronger connection between update norm, feature amplification and performance, arguing that approximately stable singular directions support directly increasing the update norm. The existing limitation requiring different scales for different backbones remains.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendices A/C newly supply extensive ranks, target layers, learning rates, schedules, batch sizes, optimizers and dataset details. These largely document previously unspecified settings. However, v2 removes the FLoRA code-access link and gives conflicting LLaVA scales: 1.5 in Section 4.3 versus 2 in Table 12.

R1.justification: Section 6.3 adds substantive distinctions from LoTR and SuperLoRA concerning layer aggregation, structural preservation and motivation. Tucker decomposition is repositioned as an aligned formulation rather than foregrounded as the starting point. New citations also support the expanded theoretical interpretation and additional benchmark comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, revises terminology throughout, moves Related Work behind the analyses and relocates the Tucker preliminaries into that section. It consolidates the theoretical/empirical discussion, expands implementation explanations and introduces organized experimental, interpretive and training appendices. This substantially changes the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to depict construction of updates from factors rather than decomposition of weights. v2 adds Figures 6-7 and Tables 4 and 6-12, compresses the retained main tables onto one page and incorporates uncertainty values into Table 3. Existing plots and the cost table are also repositioned within the conference layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves assessability and reproducibility: it supplies multimodal and generation evidence missing from the supplied v1, adds broader transfer evaluations and documents previously unspecified training settings. GLUE uncertainty reporting also strengthens the retained evidence. These gains outweigh the removed code link and conflicting LLaVA scales. The new optimality argument remains inadequately justified because its pseudoinverse construction does not guarantee exact recovery for arbitrary factor subspaces.
